name: Beam pipe
description: Your injection setup from arc 1 (Charges) is built in, but beams run in grounded metal pipes, and the pipe wall lies between the beam and your steering charge: the charge it induces on the wall cancels much of the field. Straighten the beam into the next stage again. Add a few charges.

reality.represents: A beam pipe screening a steering charge

remarks.detail: The grounded wall takes up charge that cancels much of your charge's field inside the pipe.
The pipe is a single grounded plate along one side; a real pipe surrounds the beam, and steering is done with magnets or with electrodes inside it.

remarks.line: Real plates and their fringe fields
remarks.detail: The electrodes are metal boxes standing on the plane, their surface charge solved exactly (boundary elements): uniform between plates, bulging out past their ends, and rearranging when charges come near, as in a real instrument.

Everything is symmetric about the plane z = 0, so the particle never leaves it. A real beam also has a width across the plane, where the same fields act differently (focusing in the plane can defocus across it).
